Assignment binds a name to the right-hand expression’s value; another assignment can rebind it.
Write name = value. A later right-hand expression uses a name’s current value.

annotations.text: Test the response before entering or repeating the body.

In Trace A, this repeated prompt obtains done and rebinds response before the next test.

blocks.text: The first input provides the response tested at entry. The input inside the body replaces it before the next test. A stopping response at the first prompt skips the body entirely.

blocks.text: Collect distinct color labels rather than repeated occurrences.
A set is unordered and contains distinct elements. set(items) constructs it, removing repeated values.
{item1, item2, ...} makes a nonempty set. set() makes an empty set; {} makes a dictionary.
value in values tests membership in a set.
a | b is union: elements in either set. a & b is intersection: elements in both.
Compare the label sets by membership, not display order. Repeated source labels contribute one distinct element. Union combines membership from either set; intersection keeps only shared members.
set() is an empty set, whereas {} is a dictionary. Sets do not provide stable first and second sequence positions.

annotations.text: Repeated source labels contribute one distinct element.

blocks.text: Next, choose a collection for a task.
open(path, mode) returns a file object. r reads; w writes and replaces existing contents.
Reading uses r; w replaces existing contents rather than inspecting them.

After f = open(path, "r"), f.read() reads the remaining text. After f = open(path, "w"), f.write(text) writes replacement text. If you opened f without with, call f.close() when finished; do not leave the unmanaged file open. A with block closes its file automatically after the block.

blocks.text: with open(path, mode) as f: uses an indented body and closes f after use.
f.read() reads remaining contents. f.write(text) writes text through a text-mode file object.
Without managed opening, call f.close() when finished.
Open CSV input with newline="" for the reader.
By default, csv.DictReader(f) uses the first row as dictionary keys, not a result row. list(csv.DictReader(f)) collects the row dictionaries.
The CSV header supplies keys by default; it is not returned as a data-row dictionary.
